_meta.indication: BANZEL (rufinamide) is indicated for adjunctive treatment of seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome in children 4 years and older and adults.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 022, the pivotal Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome (LGS) trial
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.phase: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized, parallel-group study
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial with a 28-day Baseline Phase followed by an 84-day (12-week) Double-blind Phase during which BANZEL or placebo was added to 1 to 3 concomitant stable-dose AEDs; target dose approximately 45 mg/kg/day
pivotal_trials.population: Male or female patients 4 to 30 years of age with inadequately controlled seizures associated with LGS (including atypical absence seizures and drop attacks) treated with 1 to 3 concomitant fixed-dose AEDs
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Three co-primary efficacy variables: percent change in total seizure frequency per 28 days, percent change in tonic-atonic (drop attack) seizure frequency per 28 days, and seizure severity from the Parent/Guardian Global Evaluation
pivotal_trials.result: Median percent change in total seizure frequency -32.7% (rufinamide) vs -11.7% (placebo), p=0.0015; median percent change in tonic-atonic (drop attack) seizure frequency -42.5% vs +1.4% increase, p<0.0001; improvement in seizure severity rating 53.4% vs 30.6%, p=0.0041

key_safety: In the pediatric LGS/adjunctive population the most common adverse reactions (>=3%, higher than placebo) included somnolence (17% vs 9%), vomiting (17% vs 7%), and headache (16% vs 8%); in adults the most common were headache (27% vs 26%), dizziness (19% vs 12%), and fatigue (16% vs 10%). Somnolence was reported in 24.3% of BANZEL-treated patients vs 12.5% of placebo patients. BANZEL also shortens the QT interval (up to 20 msec).
target_moa: The precise mechanism is unknown; in vitro studies suggest the principal mechanism is modulation of sodium channel activity, in particular prolongation of the inactive state of the channel.

rems.type: A REMS consisting of a Medication Guide and a timetable for submission of assessments was approved; the Medication Guide addresses the risk that BANZEL may increase the risk of suicidal thoughts or behavior.

orphan_indication.text: Banzel (rufinamide) for the Lennox-Gastaut syndrome indication has an orphan drug designation.

citations.quote: Because this drug for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

summary.text: NDA 21-911 for rufinamide was submitted November 17, 2005; an Approvable letter was issued September 15, 2006 and the sponsor's complete response was submitted February 29, 2008, leading to approval of the Lennox-Gastaut syndrome indication, which carries an orphan drug designation. A REMS with a Medication Guide was required.

citations.quote: The February 29, 2008 submission constituted a complete response to our September 15, 2006 action letter.
Because this drug for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

Your proposed REMS, submitted on October 24, 2008, in an electronic communication, is approved. The REMS consists of the Medication Guide included with this letter and the timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS included in your October 24, 2008 submission.

requirement.text: Conduct additional analyses to further examine the effect of Banzel (rufinamide) on the QT interval, specifically studying its effect in patients receiving concomitant medications that may also shorten the QT interval (clinical trials AE/ET1 and CRUF331-0022).

citations.quote: Conduct additional analyses to further examine the effect of Banzel (rufinamide) on the QT interval, specifically studying its effect in patients receiving concomitant medications that may also shorten the QT interval. For clinical trials AE/ET1 and CRUF331-0022 (and any other trials in which patients were treated with medications other than rufinamide and in which QT data was collected), please provide the following:The baseline (pre-treatment) mean QT interval (as measured by all three correction methods) in rufinamide-treated patients receiving concomitant drugs believed to shorten the QT interval (listed below) and in patients without such concomitant medications.

requirement.text: Conduct an in vitro metabolism study to characterize the potential serious safety risk of the inhibitory effect of Banzel (rufinamide) on P-gp.

basis.text: The Approvable letter described numerous deficiencies: effectiveness data in partial seizures gave inconsistent results and small treatment effects, several nonclinical studies were inadequate, and the proposed tradename was unacceptable.
